body:
Market valuations affect which engine you can rely on. In mid-November 2026 the Nifty 50 traded at about **20.6x trailing earnings**. Midcap forward P/E was close to its 10-year average (22.8x vs 23.2x). **Small-cap forward P/E stood at 21.9x against a 10-year average of 18.7x** ([HDFC MF](https://www.hdfcfund.com/learn/deep-dives/tuesday-talking-point/equity-valuations-remain-reasonable-despite-market-uptick)). These figures change constantly, so re-check them. With small caps still at a premium, new small-cap bets need **earnings delivery rather than further rerating** to work. Cycle history warns against buying a theme at its peak multiple. The BSE Capital Goods index took **14 years to regain its 2007 peak** ([Business Standard](https://business-standard.com/article/markets/bse-capital-goods-index-hits-fresh-52-week-high-l-t-bel-gain-up-to-3-120121400412_1.html)).

body:
Radhakishan Damani came from a broking family. His father was on Dalal Street, and after his father's death he left a ball-bearings business to join his brother's broking firm ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/rakesh-jhunjunwala-guru-radhakishan-damani-second-richest-mukesh-ambani/story/396422.html)). That background was the information edge in a small ring-trading market. In the early 1990s he was short while Harshad Mehta pushed prices up, and later he shorted stocks Mehta promoted "until they fell" ([Rediff](https://www.rediff.com/business/special/how-well-do-you-know-d-marts-damani/20170405.htm)). Folklore says the short nearly bankrupted him before the scam broke and links him to Manu Manek's "bear cartel". Neither claim has a primary source, so treat both as legend. He then moved to long holdings: HDFC Bank at its 1995 listing, VST, Gillette and Crisil. His line on paying up for quality was that you can't live on Peddar Road at Dharavi's rates ([Rediff](https://www.rediff.com/business/special/how-well-do-you-know-d-marts-damani/20170405.htm)).

The decisive move was leaving the market around 2000 to build D-Mart. He owned his stores rather than leasing them, priced everyday groceries about 8% below retail, turned inventory 3–4x faster than peers and paid vendors in about 10 days. He expanded slowly: about 10 stores when Big Bazaar had 250 ([Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/lead-story/radhakishan-damani-the-slow-and-steady-retail-king-6675)). At the 2017 IPO his **~82% stake was worth over ₹32,000 crore, about 90% of his net worth** ([Rediff](https://www.rediff.com/business/special/how-well-do-you-know-d-marts-damani/20170405.htm)). His roughly $14–16 billion today rises and falls with D-Mart's valuation ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radhakishan_Damani)). The honest lesson from Damani is about running a business on cost discipline and owned assets. It is not about stock-picking.

body:
Every legend had a structural edge, not just knowledge:
- Buffett: tiny capital in an unscreened market; read Moody's manuals page by page;
  later ~1.7x leverage via insurance float cheaper than T-bills; never forced to sell.
- Lynch: 200+ company visits & ~700 annual reports/yr; pre-Reg FD private access.
- Damani: broking-family networks; 1992 short side; ~90% of wealth = D-Mart founder stake.
- Jhunjhunwala: borrowed client money early; 1992 bear trade; Titan ~1/3 of wealth.
- Prop firms/FPIs: speed, algos, option-selling at scale; took ~₹58k cr from F&O in FY26
  while individuals lost (SEBI).
Knowledge alone is commoditised. Edge = information processed differently, over time,
plus temperament and survival.

body:
1. **Depth standard ("security-guard depth").** A friend researching Vishal Mega Mart checked even what
   security guards are paid. Match that *depth* (not that exact fact): store/unit economics, cost lines,
   staffing, rent, supplier terms, customer behaviour, competitor economics, ground reality — the level
   big investors reach. Learning also means non-stock knowledge (industries, economics, psychology, data).
2. **Context over checklists.** Not all bad numbers are bad and not all good numbers are good until we know
   the real story. 100x P/E with every metric "against" it has still skyrocketed. Learn — company by company
   — which red flags to ignore and which green flags are traps. Never let a checklist replace judgment.
3. **Markets:** India slightly more weight, US close behind; neither ignored. Go where the best is.
4. **Work mode:** no scheduled task for now; keep working continuously; the user will prompt after
   usage limits reset. Requirements list lives in `My Requirements/requirements.md`.
